- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially after sharp spikes.
- If model shows gradual upward trend but true outcome drops sharply (e.g., >10% drop in 3–5 days), reduce forecast slope and add mean-reversion component.
- After a strong bullish sentiment spike, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2 standard deviations above recent high.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model continues upward, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid “sentiment mismatch” bias.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >15% from forecast mean, check sentiment history for recent reversal signals — adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often fails to capture turning points; use sentiment momentum as a lagged filter to adjust forecast direction.
